title: WPSS/1552/2019 of MAHENDRA SINGH NEGI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
WPSS No. 1552 of 2019
Hon'ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. Deep Chandra Joshi, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Atul Bahuguna, Brief Holder for the State of
Uttarakhand.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Petitioner is serving as Junior Clerk in Education
Department and he was posted at Government Inter College
Bullawala, Doiwala, Dehradun. He was transferred to
Government Inter College, Kwasi, Chakrata, Dehradun vide
order dated 25.06.2019. Thus, feeling aggrieved, petitioner
has approached this Court.
According to learned counsel for the petitioner,
petitioner is suffering from permanent disability to the extent
of 40%, therefore, he could not have been transferred in view
of the provisions contained in Transfer Act, 2017. He further
submits that petitioner was recently transferred to the present
place of posting and he has now been transferred within six
months of his joining at the present place. He further submits
that petitioner has served for nearly nine years at a Durgam
school.
Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the
case, this Court thinks that ends of justice would be met, if
petitioner is permitted to make a representation to the
Competent Authority, which shall be decided by him, within
some specified time frame.
 Accordingly, the writ petition is disposed of with
liberty to petitioner to make representation to Competent
Authority within one week from today. If such representation
is made, Competent Authority shall look into the matter and
shall take appropriate decision by passing a speaking order, in
accordance with law, within three weeks from the date of
receipt of representation alongwith certified copy of this
order.
It is further provided that for a period of four weeks or
till decision on representation of the petitioner, whichever is
earlier, status quo shall be maintained regarding posting of the
petitioner.
Since, this Court has not considered the validity of the
transfer order on merits; therefore, it shall be open to the
petitioner to challenge the transfer order by filing another writ
petition, in case his representation is decided against him.
